chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.text: Field Journal. Chapter one. Arrival at the north ridge. Morgan reached the field station shortly after sunrise. The road was dry, but the valley was covered in mist. Before leaving the vehicle, the team checked the sample bags, spare batteries, and the paper map. Each person wrote the date in a separate notebook. At the first outcrop, Morgan found dark basalt beside a narrow stream. No samples were collected yet. The team first photographed the exposed rock and marked the location. This chapter ends at the north ridge. The next chapter follows the return route through the valley.

chapters.title: Return
chapters.text: Field Journal. Chapter two. Return through the valley. The afternoon walk began at the narrow stream. Morgan counted twelve sealed bags and checked every label against the notebook. One label was difficult to read, so the team stopped and replaced it before continuing. At the bridge they met Avery, who was carrying a separate collection from the southern basin. The collections stayed in different boxes. Back at the station, both teams compared their notes and planned the next survey. The north ridge report was complete, but the instrument calibration still needed another check. This is the end of the field journal.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.text: Weather Notes. Chapter one. Arrival of the coastal front. Avery opened the shutters and looked toward the sea. Clouds were moving inland, while the ground near the station was still dry. The first reading was taken before breakfast. The second reading was taken after the wind changed direction. Avery recorded the measurements in the weather log, not in the geological field journal. By midday, a thin band of rain had reached the western hill. The team moved the outdoor equipment under cover and waited for the front to pass. The next chapter describes the clear evening that followed.

chapters.title: Return
chapters.text: Weather Notes. Chapter two. Return of clear skies. After sunset, the rain stopped and the clouds began to separate. Avery checked the outdoor instruments and compared the evening readings with the morning log. A small pool remained beside the gate, but the eastern path was dry. The team reopened the shutters and prepared the equipment for the following day. No geological samples were moved during this inspection. The weather log stayed on the desk beside the window. Before turning off the light, Avery recorded one final observation: the coastal front had passed, and the night was calm.

chapters.title: Station Log
chapters.text: Station Log. This is a separate single file recording. At the end of the survey, the station manager checked the equipment cupboard. Two maps were returned to the upper shelf. The north and south sample boxes were stored separately. Spare batteries remained in the drawer beside the radio. The manager signed the daily register and placed it next to the entrance. Tomorrow the teams will leave at different times, so each team must check the gate key before departure. This station log is not a chapter of the field journal or the weather notes. End of recording.
